lines: France's top literary prize just went to a novel that used ChatGPT.
Yes, really. The author said so himself.
A day after winning, the author went on French radio.
He said he turned to AI three times while writing.
One was a sentence written by ChatGPT, added to play with the reader.
Another made fun of how absurd its answers can be.
But the jury only heard about it on the day of the award.
He told the jurors, and he joked about it.
Online, people split. Some said it is just a tool.
Others asked why a novelist would need it.
His view is that you cannot ignore AI.
He said we must acknowledge it, and tame it.
Three uses, inside one whole novel.
So where is the line between a tool and a coauthor?
A spellchecker fixes words. ChatGPT can write whole sentences.
If a novel you loved used ChatGPT once, would you still read it?
